automatic_no_go.description: Any duplicate externally visible lifecycle effect.
A stale generation performs a destructive effect.
A restricted secret appears in evidence or telemetry.
The internal/operator listener is publicly reachable.

scenarios.title: Disabled-path compatibility
scenarios.description: Celld defaults off without changing existing QEMU, Docker, or host behavior.
given: AGENTIC_CELLD_ENABLED is absent or false and non-Celld fixtures exist.
when: The focused Celld units and full existing lifecycle regression suites run.
then: worker-celld is unavailable, no Celld endpoint is contacted, and existing runtimes remain operable.

assertions.expected: Focused disabled configuration and discovery units pass.
Zero requests reach a Celld endpoint while disabled.
All prior QEMU, Docker, and host lifecycle outcomes pass unchanged.

cleanup: Stop disposable runtimes and prove the original fixture inventory remains operable.

scenarios.title: Contract, version, and authority fail closed
scenarios.description: Versioned contracts and authority rules reject ambiguous or incompatible inputs before effects.
given: The v1 schemas, canonical examples, authority model, and pinned compatibility pair are present.
when: Static contract, digest, version, and authority coverage checks run.
then: Schemas and pins agree, unknown versions fail closed, and each shared field has one authority and repair rule.
prerequisites: committed Celld contracts and reference manifests

assertions.expected: All three v1 schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12 objects with stable identifiers.
Celld, protocol, and reference Worker digest pins match across manifests.
Every shared field has exactly one authority and a repair rule in machine-readable evidence.

cleanup: No cleanup is required for read-only contract validation.

scenarios.title: Duplicate delivery and idempotency
scenarios.description: Repeated and concurrent delivery creates one provider effect per operation identity.
given: Fresh InstanceCells and instrumented QEMU and Docker providers are available.
when: Each lifecycle command is delivered 10000 times with the same operation ID and request hash.
then: All replays resolve to one ledger record and one externally visible provider effect.

assertions.expected: Exactly one provider effect per operation ID across 10000 repeats per action and substrate.
Operation ID reuse with a different request hash is rejected.

cleanup: Destroy disposable generations once and verify retained tombstones.

scenarios.title: Acknowledged-intent restart and owner loss
scenarios.description: Management and Celld owner crashes cannot lose acknowledged intent or duplicate effects.
given: Pinned live QEMU and Docker fleets expose management and owner kill controls.
when: Each owner is killed before, during, and after dispatch for 100 trials per crash point and substrate.
then: The original operation resumes and desired and observed state converge.

assertions.expected: 100 percent of acknowledged intents survive all crash points.
Recovery p95 is at most 30 seconds with zero duplicate effects.

cleanup: Restore every killed component and verify healthy membership and inventory.

scenarios.title: Timeout and unknown-outcome recovery
scenarios.description: A lost response becomes unknown and is repaired by lookup, never by a second effect.
given: A provider proxy can drop management responses after effects complete.
when: Responses are dropped for 100 trials per action and substrate and reconciliation runs.
then: The original operation ID is looked up and reaches a terminal state without a second effect.

assertions.expected: Every lookup and retry reuses the original operation ID.
Zero second provider effects and p95 convergence at most 30 seconds.

cleanup: Remove fault rules and prove normal request delivery resumes.

scenarios.title: Generation fencing and tombstones
scenarios.description: Stale and future actors cannot affect the active generation.
given: Generation N is tombstoned and the logical instance is reprovisioned as N+1.
when: Delayed destructive commands for N and future commands for N+2 arrive after partition recovery.
then: Every command is rejected before the provider and N+1 remains active.

assertions.expected: 100 stale stop and destroy trials per substrate are rejected before provider invocation.
The active N+1 generation never changes because of stale or future commands.

cleanup: Heal the partition and reconcile only the active generation.

scenarios.title: Claimed Worker capability surface
scenarios.description: Every advertised Worker capability works on the pinned runtime within its declared limits.
given: The reference bundle is deployed to pinned Celld with immutable digest evidence.
when: Fetch, RPC, storage, alarms, WebSocket, outbound HTTPS, Wasm, and asset cases run.
then: Every advertised capability passes and rollback to the prior digest succeeds.

assertions.expected: 100 percent of advertised capability conformance cases pass.
Pinned rollback restores the prior digest without lost durable state.

cleanup: Restore the approved reference digest and verify durable state.

scenarios.title: Unsupported Worker capabilities fail loudly
scenarios.description: OS, raw-network, agent, and hostile-tenancy claims are rejected without side effects.
given: Malicious bundles attempt every explicitly excluded capability.
when: Validation, deployment, discovery, and 100 runtime attempts per capability execute.
then: Each attempt returns a typed rejection and creates no process, file, socket, VM, or container.

assertions.expected: All excluded capabilities fail loudly on every attempt.
Zero host processes, files, sockets, containers, or VMs are created.

cleanup: Remove malicious bundles and verify fleet health.

scenarios.title: Worker resource containment
scenarios.description: Resource-limit violations contain only the offending isolate.
given: Two healthy workloads and one adversarial workload run on the reference fleet.
when: CPU, memory, request, storage, resident-cell, and outbound limits are exceeded independently.
then: Only the offender is throttled or terminated and the fleet stays healthy.

assertions.expected: The offender is enforced within 5 seconds or one request interval and no node crashes.
Adjacent workload success remains at least 99 percent.

cleanup: Terminate the adversarial isolate and prove resources return below baseline thresholds.

scenarios.title: Object-store and topology preflight
scenarios.description: Storage semantics and listener isolation must pass before provisioning.
given: A dedicated scoped prefix and three-node private-overlay fleet exist.
when: Conditional races, consistency, latency, scope denial, and reachability probes run.
then: Preflight passes only complete semantics and no forbidden route or prefix is reachable.

assertions.expected: Zero split owners in 10000 races and object-store p99 at most 250 ms.
100 percent of public, cross-fleet, and cross-prefix access attempts are denied.

cleanup: Delete only the disposable preflight namespace and retain the fleet bucket.

scenarios.title: Rolling update, rollback, and node loss
scenarios.description: A three-node fleet preserves reserve and durable intent during updates and failures.
given: Three nodes, reserve one, max unavailable one, and old/new qualified artifacts are installed.
when: One-node batches roll, a node is killed, rollback triggers, and an unknown pair is proposed.
then: Budgets hold, state rebuilds, rollback succeeds, and the unknown pair is refused before drain.

assertions.expected: Unavailable nodes never exceed one and declared reserve is never consumed.
Zero lost intents, duplicate effects, or stale effects; p95 reconciliation at most 30 seconds.
An incompatible pair changes zero nodes before refusal.

cleanup: Return every node to the approved digest and restore reserve capacity.

scenarios.title: Control-plane authentication and isolation
scenarios.description: Forged, stale, replayed, wrong-generation, and forbidden-route requests have no effect.
given: Signed request fixtures and an observable provider boundary exist.
when: One valid and 1000 attempts of each negative request class are sent.
then: Only the valid request reaches the provider and every denial is typed and observable.

assertions.expected: 100 percent of negative attempts are denied with zero provider effects.
The valid control request succeeds and is correlated without signature disclosure.

cleanup: Revoke disposable signing identities and remove probe firewall rules.

scenarios.title: Credential, provenance, and rotation hygiene
scenarios.description: Scoped credentials rotate without leakage or provenance downgrade.
given: Unique canary secrets, old/new scoped references, and immutable signed artifacts are prepared.
when: Deploy, diagnostics, evidence capture, cross-prefix access, rotation, and failed-canary rollback run.
then: No canary leaks, scope does not broaden, overlap is bounded, and digest mismatch blocks install.

assertions.expected: Zero canary secret occurrences outside protected credential files.
All cross-prefix attempts fail and credential overlap is at most 15 minutes.
Any version, digest, signature, or commit mismatch blocks installation.

cleanup: Revoke disposable credentials and confirm the approved identity remains active.

scenarios.title: Diagnostics, alerts, and repair honesty
scenarios.description: Operators can distinguish failed boundaries and a repair plan never claims an unproven effect.
given: One injectable fault exists for each management, Celld, store, provider, divergence, and fleet boundary.
when: CLI, API, dashboard, telemetry, and alerts are queried after each isolated fault.
then: Every boundary is correctly classified and all evidence carries required correlation fields.

assertions.expected: 100 percent of injected faults identify the correct failed boundary.
Every applicable record contains fleet, instance, generation, operation, trace, version, and node identities.
Divergence alerts after 5 minutes, unknown after two intervals, and stale generation within one evaluation interval.

cleanup: Heal every injected fault and verify all alerts resolve.

scenarios.title: Backup, restore, and idempotent runbooks
scenarios.description: Versioned recovery preserves generations and is safe to repeat.
given: Versioned snapshots, retained tombstones, and an isolated restore prefix exist.
when: Node loss, full restart, auth loss, snapshot restore, and rotation runbooks execute twice.
then: Latest generations reconcile without duplicate effects and evidence is independently readable.

assertions.expected: Measured RPO is at most 300 seconds and RTO at most 30 minutes.
Second runbook execution creates zero additional lifecycle effects.
Independent evidence hashes verify after affected-fleet loss.

cleanup: Quarantine the restore fleet and retain recovery evidence according to policy.

scenarios.title: Capacity, soak, cost, and independent lane verdicts
scenarios.description: A real 24-hour load run proves SLOs, headroom, cost visibility, and separate support decisions.
given: A three-node reference fleet runs 1000 resident cells per node at 50 lifecycle operations per second.
when: Actual wall-clock load runs for 24 hours with a planned node loss and recovery.
then: SLOs and headroom pass, costs are separated, and the three product lanes receive independent verdicts.

assertions.expected: p99 acceptance is at most 250 ms, p99 convergence at most 30 seconds, and error rate below 1 percent.
Zero duplicate effects or lost intents over the full 24 hours.
CPU and memory retain 30 percent headroom and Celld costs are separated by component and substrate.

cleanup: Stop generated load and return fleet utilization to its recorded baseline.

scenarios.title: Human operator acceptance
scenarios.description: Representative operators can diagnose, reconcile, rollback, and export evidence safely without author assistance.
given: Runbooks and the CLI, API, and dashboard from the operational scenarios are available.
when: At least one representative per role executes the critical workflows and records structured feedback.
then: Workflow pass rate and satisfaction meet the UAT gate with no critical issue.

assertions.expected: At least 90 percent of critical workflows pass first execution.
Mean satisfaction is at least 4 of 5 with zero critical usability defects.
Every destructive action displays the target instance and generation before confirmation.

cleanup: Restore the disposable fleet and preserve only consented, redacted UAT evidence.
